newsitem.title: UK: Lower De La Rue profits drag shr price down.
newsitem.headline: Lower De La Rue profits drag shr price down.

text.p: British printing and security products group De La Rue Plc was among the biggest losers on the London stock market on Tuesday after its 1996/97 annual profits fell below expectations and the company ruled out any immediate improvement.

The company's share price tumbled 54 1/2 pence or 11.24 percent to 430p before noon after reporting a pretax, pre-exceptional profits of 120.2 million pounds ($196.4 million) against 147.9 million in the previous year.
The figures even fell short of the bottom end of analysts' expectations which ranged between 124 million pounds and 129.5 million.
"The market wasn't too pleased by the figures to say the least," one trader said.
"The company says it will do better after the reorganisation but that is going to take some time yet," he said.
The company's sales was marginally ahead, by 0.6 percent, to 768.2 million pounds while its earnings per share dipped to 35 pence from a previous 50.5 pence.
The company recommended a dividend of 24.0 pence per share, almost unchanged from last year's 23.75 pence per share.
Nevertheless, the company's chief executive, Jeremy Marshall, promised medium to long term growth on current investments that were being made in its cash systems and smart card divisions.
He said that this was a temporary phase and the company needed at least another couple of years before it could show steady growth.
"We are taking the pain now in order to build on a stronger platform," Marshall told Reuters in an interview.
"Sales of newly developed products (in cash systems) are expected to increase, particularly towards the end of the financial year," Marshall said.
He said the division's profit was expected to grow during the current year.
Adverse exchange rates and lower sales on products with higher profit margins had pulled down the company's operating profits from this division to 22.1 million pounds from 38.0 million.
The company is investing a significant portion of its expenditure on developing 20 new cash systems products. "We are pretty sure about very good returns from them," he said.
"One would expect the volumes to pick up in a couple of years," he said.

The company expects to invest more in developing the cash systems market in some of the emerging economies like India, China, the Ukraine, Poland and Russia, currently witnessing sweeping banking reforms including automation.
It is also banking on its recent 54-million pound acquisition of Philips Smart Cards and Systems.
De La Rue's forecast, Marshall said, was that the smart card market would treble from a $1.0 billion today to more than $3.0 billion by the turn of the century.

The company is currently reorganising its bank note printing division which showed a decline of 7.5 percent in sales during the year mainly due to overcapacity in the sector which led to pressured on margins.
"In these tough market conditions, costs associated with higher specification notes have not been fully recovered in sales prices," the company said in a statement.
De La Rue's profit margins from its security paper and printing fell to 20.6 percent from 24.5 percent in the previous year.
The company acquired another smaller printer, Harrison & Sons, earlier this year and embarked on a reorganisation of its UK security print operations.
The reorganisation is expected to be completed by the end 1997 with the company expected to benefit of about seven million pounds annually after that.
"We have a very clear strategy and we believe that the investments we are making now will give us very good growth in the medium term future," Marshall said.
($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
